# Native Floating-Root Feedback and Frozen-Torque Replay (Provisional)

## Exact Native State and Controller Law

F02 child #11946 connects the existing distributed-feedback law to the F05c
MuJoCo 3.8.0 floating-root, two-hinge plant. The compiled fixture has
$n_q=9$, $n_v=8$, $n_u=2$ and an Euler step of $0.01\,\mathrm{s}$. The six
root tangent coordinates have no actuators; two named direct unit motors drive
the hip and knee. This fixture is contact-free and gravity-free. The
adapter reuses F05c native topology, motor, integrator, initial-state and
hidden-force admission before a controller command is accepted.

At each native integration boundary, the F02 controller reads the simulated
$(q_k,v_k)$ once. Its configuration error is the MuJoCo tangent operation

$$
e_q=\operatorname{mj\_differentiatePos}(q_k^*,q_k;\Delta t=1)
\in\mathbb R^8,
\qquad e_v=v_k-v_k^*.
$$

The argument order is **reference then current**, yielding the F02
current-minus-reference convention. The unit time argument makes this a
configuration difference, rather than a physical velocity. The native
quaternion is validated as normalized; $q$ and $-q$ produce the same rotation
error. No four-component quaternion subtraction is used. MuJoCo's sparse
mass matrix is expanded at the current configuration and inverted for F02's
positive-definite tangent inverse-mass contract. The nominal gain is the
existing MOSAIC TVLQR gain on the 16-dimensional
$[e_q,e_v]$ tangent, with the same native Euler discrete derivative as F05c.

The applied input is the existing F02 law with frozen feedforward, optional
feedback, explicit motor map, native `ctrlrange` saturation and a declared
per-motor rate limit. The root cannot receive a requested generalized effort.
The code retains $u^{\rm ff}$, feedback correction, total requested effort
and post-limit motor torque as separate per-step evidence. Disabled feedback
executes the same frozen nominal schedule for a paired comparison; it does
not alter the plant or nominal input.

## Execution and Independent Replay

The common native torque runner calls the controller once per Euler step and
holds its **actual post-limit actuator torque** by zero-order hold. It exports
the executed channel order, exact integration grid and complete
`mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` initial state through pinned Tools T01. A fresh MuJoCo
instance receives only that time-only torque history. It never calls the
feedback controller, observes the controlled run or resets to later states.
Every native configuration, velocity and full integration-state row must
match the closed-loop run within $10^{-12}$ or the run fails. This is a
same-model frozen-input reproduction result, not motion-capture accuracy.

The synthetic 12-step fixture starts with a $0.4\,\mathrm{rad}$ hip error.
The native manifold TVLQR run reduces its final hip error relative to the
frozen-zero-input run. A separate overdrive test requests $(4,-4)$ N m but
the compiled bounds yield exactly $(2,-1.5)$ N m in both the saved bundle
and independent replay. Negative tests reject channel permutation,
unnormalized quaternion and contact geometry. Tests run against actual
MuJoCo 3.8.0, not an algebraic stand-in. The source-hashed receipt and
reproduction command are in the F02 native turnover document.

The same adapter also consumes a **moving reference** obtained by executing
an admissible, varying two-motor ZOH history in an independent native replay.
It differentiates each actual native Euler transition in the 16-dimensional
tangent and runs the existing MOSAIC Riccati pass; the resulting
`NominalTrajectory` contains the replayed $(q_k,v_k)$ and teacher
feedforward torque. The fixture is autonomous, so local differentiation may
normalize the otherwise complete saved state's time coordinate to zero;
each differentiated successor is checked against the recorded native
successor. This time normalization is not admitted for time-dependent
callbacks or external drives.

Feedback admission and independent replay use the same
`require_no_global_mujoco_callbacks` inspection boundary. A missing callback
getter or an installed callback rejects admission before evaluation; the
feedback adapter does not maintain a separate private callback-name list.

From one held-out $0.25\,\mathrm{rad}$ hip perturbation, a frozen-feedforward
run and an exact-state feedback run use the **same** native model, initial
state, input grid and policy. The frozen run's saved input hash equals the
teacher history; the feedback run's applied-input hash differs. Their final
hip errors against the moving teacher are $0.07508$ and $0.02460\,\mathrm{rad}$,
respectively. Both separate complete-state replays match exactly in this
fixture. The test retains both histories; no optimizer or fitting success
is inferred from a teacher-created reference. F03's current sparse
collocation spike is one-dimensional and does not export a native 9/8/2
solution into this boundary.

This only qualifies a software boundary and local synthetic fixture.
Human anatomy, gravity/contact/grip, state-dependent transmissions, muscle
excitation, marker observation, private capture, production perturbations,
full swing, six-engine parity and a scientific runtime deadline remain open.
The F02 and F05 parents and the manual release remain blocked.
